CONDITIONAL: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 17, audited at commit 3d53396 (HEAD of the main checkout). Sprint
file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. Eight files, 612 insertions.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL PASS. One required fix. Everything else is met, and the two
criteria this sprint named as mattering most -- the write surface and the API key --
are both met well.

REQUIRED FIX -- the prompt tells the model that every aspect is separating, and the
test suite is built so that cannot be seen.

The chain, each step verified rather than assumed:
  1. composeChart calls computeAspects(positions, positions) -- Sprint 15, documented,
     and the reason is sound: R4 there forbids recomputing positions inside it.
     Consequence: every aspect it returns has applying: false, mechanically.
  2. app/reading/[id]/actions.ts builds readingModel.chart from composeChart.
  3. generateHoroscope -> buildPrompt renders
     `${a.applying ? "applying" : "separating"}`.
Therefore every aspect in every production prompt reads "separating".

PRD §5's own worked example, for this project's own fixture date, lists four of the
top six as applying:
    Saturn square Uranus — orb 0.89°, applying
    Mars trine Uranus — orb 2.05°, applying
    Sun opposition Pluto — orb 2.23°, applying
    Saturn sextile Pluto — orb 2.83°, applying
The prompt this code assembles will label all four separating. And §5's expected
output hangs its second paragraph on exactly one of them -- "Saturn in Leo squared
Uranus in Scorpio at less than a degree, still closing." Still closing is applying.
The system prompt then says "Invent no astrological data beyond what is supplied" and
"Commit to it. No hedging, no 'may have'". So the model will not hedge: it will
confidently assert the opposite of the PRD's own worked example, in the demo this
whole proof of concept exists to give.

What makes this a required fix rather than a note is that it was written down in
advance, aimed at this sprint by name. docs/design/CHART_MODEL.md, committed in
Sprint 15, says: "Whoever wires up Sprint 17's prompt template (which does plan to
show applying/separating) needs a real second snapshot from somewhere and should not
read this field as meaningful before then." That instruction is not followed and is
not addressed anywhere in this diff. I am not inventing a requirement; I am pointing
at a committed one.

And the tests conceal it. lib/llm/horoscope.test.ts's fixture hand-builds a
ReadingModel with applying: true on four aspects -- a ReadingModel that composeChart,
the only producer of ChartModel in this codebase, cannot construct. So the test
"labels applying/separating per aspect" passes by asserting
`"Saturn square Uranus — orb 0.89°, applying"` against input that never occurs, while
production emits the opposite string for that exact line. buildPrompt is correct; the
suite proves it against a shape nothing produces, which is worse than not testing it,
because it reads as coverage.

Two fixes are available, both inside this sprint's own code, neither needing a PRD
amendment. I am not choosing between them:
  - Compute a real second snapshot in app/reading/[id]/actions.ts and pass real
    aspects. Sprint 15's R4 forbids recomputation inside composeChart -- not in the
    action -- and a t+1h snapshot used only to derive a boolean is never displayed and
    never stored, so it cannot make a saved reading disagree with its row. That is the
    "real second snapshot from somewhere" CHART_MODEL.md asked for.
  - Or omit the label from the prompt until it can be computed. Strictly better than
    false data: it removes a claim rather than adding one, and it is trivially
    reversible.
Whichever is chosen, reconcile the test fixture: it should be a shape composeChart can
actually produce, or say in the file why it deliberately is not.

Requirements coverage:
R1 MET. generateHoroscope(reading: ReadingModel): Promise<{text, model}>, temperature
  0.9, asserted in the request body by test.
R2 MET as its criterion is written -- top 6, not 15, with a test proving the 7th and
  8th are dropped, and two-decimal rounding on both positions and orbs. The "invent no
  astrological data" rule is present verbatim. See the required fix for the value of
  one field the template renders.
R3 MET, and carefully. set_reading_horoscope is security definer with
  set search_path = public, the same hardening get_reading_by_id carries and for the
  same stated reason. It sets exactly horoscope, horoscope_generated_at and
  horoscope_model, takes no column name, no JSON patch and no arbitrary fields, and
  horoscope_generated_at comes from now() inside the function rather than from a
  parameter, so a caller cannot backdate it. The parameter names deliberately collide
  with column names and every body reference is qualified as
  set_reading_horoscope.<name>, which is what keeps the UPDATE unambiguous rather than
  silently resolving to a column -- the comment says so, which is the part that stops
  someone "simplifying" it later. returns boolean with returning true means a
  nonexistent id yields NULL rather than a silent success, and the caller checks it.
R4 MET, checked as the named absence it is. Grepped every migration for create policy,
  alter policy and "for update": the only policy statement in the entire migration set
  is still Sprint 4's insert policy. Sprint 4's deny-update property survives.
R5 MET, and verified by execution rather than by reading. OPENAI_API_KEY is never
  NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed and is read in exactly one place, resolveOpenAiConfig. Its
  module is imported only by lib/llm/generate.ts, which is imported only by a
  "use server" action and a server component -- and there is no "use client" anywhere
  in this repository at all. Then the real check: built with
  OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-QA1PROBEOPENAIKEY" and grepped the entire .next output. Absent.
  So is the service role key, still.
R6 MET. `HOROSCOPE_ENABLED?.trim().toLowerCase() !== "false"` -- absent means enabled,
  a typo means enabled, only an explicit false disables. Three tests cover exactly
  those three cases. The feature cannot ship silently off, which is what the
  requirement was for.
R7 MET. Generation runs only from the button's form submission; nothing on the
  reading-creation path calls it. The action re-fetches the row by id rather than
  trusting hidden form fields for positions and events, so a crafted POST cannot shape
  the prompt -- that is a hardening the requirement did not ask for and it closes a
  real vector on a path that spends money. The button reads "Regenerate horoscope"
  when one already exists, which is where R7's explicit-request distinction lives.
R8 MET, and the asymmetry with Sprint 16 is implemented deliberately rather than
  inconsistently -- horoscope.ts's own comment states why this one throws where the
  event fetch degrades. Non-2xx, missing content and timeout all throw; the RPC is
  only reached after generateHoroscope resolves, so there is no partial-write path,
  only ordering, and the comment says that too. Separate tests cover a generation
  failure and a persistence failure, and the persistence-failure test asserts no false
  success.
R9 MET. Minimal unstyled button, the disabled state says so plainly, errors render in
  a role="alert" paragraph.
R10 MET, grepped as the criterion demands. Every test stubs fetch. The only
  api.openai.com string in a test file is an assertion that the mocked fetch was called
  with the right URL.
R11 MET. Prompt assembly including both the top-6 and rounding rules, the disabled
  path, API failure surfacing, and the persisted columns on success.
No DDL outside supabase/migrations/; the ledger insert is present and matches the
  filename.

Verified by execution:
- lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 147 tests across 15 files, 19 new.
- next build exits 0; route table unchanged.
- The R5 probe above.

Notes, not conditions:
1. set_reading_horoscope is granted to anon, so anyone holding a reading id can write
   arbitrary text into that reading's horoscope directly over the Data API, without
   going near OpenAI. R3 requires the anon grant, so this is not a deviation, and it is
   consistent with the model Sprint 4 established -- the link is the access control,
   and the holder of a link could already create their own reading. But it is worth
   recording as a decision rather than a side effect: a tighter shape existed. Granting
   the function to service_role only and calling it from the server action with
   createAdminClient would have made this write genuinely server-only while changing
   nothing a user can see. Worth knowing which you chose, since the stored horoscope is
   currently not guaranteed to be model output.
2. generate.ts's `catch { return { ok: false, ... } }` discards the OpenAI error
   entirely. R8 requires surfacing to the user and that is done -- but nothing records
   why. This is the same thing Sprint 16 promoted to R12, and the case is stronger
   here: this path fails for quota, rate limit and billing reasons, which are exactly
   the failures you diagnose from logs and cannot diagnose from "Horoscope generation
   failed, try again."
3. app/reading/[id]/actions.ts interpolates readingId into the redirect path without
   encoding. I checked whether it can escape the origin: it cannot, because the
   /reading/ prefix means even a value starting with // stays origin-relative. So this
   is not an open redirect and I am not raising it as one. Worst case is a redirect to
   an odd same-origin path. encodeURIComponent would match what saveReading already
   does with its own parameters.
4. The page reflects searchParams.error into the markup. React escapes it, so text
   only -- the same reflected-text note I have carried since Sprint 3, unchanged in
   severity.
5. Accepted per Out of Scope, restated so the record is explicit: a public
   unauthenticated button that costs money per press, no rate limiting, with the spend
   cap and the kill switch as the only controls. The kill switch works without a
   redeploy, which is the property that makes that acceptable.

Re-audit after the applying decision lands. Whichever way it goes it is a small change
in one or two files plus the test fixture; keep the re-audit proportionate to that.

PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 17, round 2. Audited at commit c3bf6fa, HEAD of the main checkout,
recorded tree 64fe6889... Sprint file re-read fresh; unchanged, so the criteria are
the ones I audited against in round 1. Scope: four files.

VERDICT: PASS.

REQUIRED FIX -- the applying/separating label. FIXED, and fixed the harder of the two
ways I offered.

computePromptAspects(eventDate, positions) computes a real one-day-later snapshot and
calls computeAspects(storedPositions, laterPositions). The now side stays the
persisted positions -- only the later snapshot is recomputed -- so the property
Sprint 15's R4 exists to protect is untouched: nothing displayed or stored is
recalculated, and the recomputed snapshot exists only to derive a boolean. orb,
tightness, aspect and sort order all derive from the stored side, so they are
bit-identical to what composeChart produced; only `applying` changes. The comment
states the scoping argument -- R4 constrains composeChart, not every caller -- rather
than leaving someone to reconstruct it.

The verification is what makes this convincing. The new test asserts all fifteen
aspects against CHART_MODEL.md's own Application column, `applying` included. I
checked that fixture against the committed document row by row: Sun-Saturn separating,
Saturn-Uranus applying, Mars-Uranus applying, Sun-Pluto applying, Moon-Venus
separating, Saturn-Pluto applying, and so on through all fifteen. It matches exactly,
and it passes. So the fix is verified against the very document that raised the
problem, which is the strongest form this could take -- and CHART_MODEL.md's warning
block, written in Sprint 15 and aimed at this sprint by name, is now satisfied rather
than outstanding.

The second new test closes the gap I actually complained about in round 1, which was
that the suite could not see the defect: it spies on generateHoroscope and asserts the
ReadingModel it receives has at least one applying aspect. Before the fix that
assertion was structurally impossible to satisfy. That is the test that would have
caught this, and it now exists.

On the one-day step: the constant is named APPLYING_SNAPSHOT_STEP_MS and the comment
records that it matches adapter.ts's RETROGRADE_STEP_DAYS and the method
CHART_MODEL.md's Application column was generated with. That is the right call for
consistency -- the prompt now agrees with the project's own reference document and
with PRD §5's worked example. My Sprint 12 measurement stands unchanged (a one-hour
step disagrees with a one-day step on roughly one verdict in nine, and I judged the
shorter step more accurate), but that is now a single named constant rather than an
implicit choice, and changing it would mean changing CHART_MODEL.md's recorded table
too. Deliberate, documented, consistent. Not my call to reopen.

A side benefit worth crediting: buildReadingModel moved out of the "use server" file
into lib/llm/generate.ts, and the action's own comment says why -- so that it stays
covered by generate.test.ts rather than living untested behind a server-action
boundary. The action is now nine lines shorter and does only what a server action
should: read the form, fetch the row, delegate, redirect.

Round 1's coverage of R1 through R11 stands. I re-verified the parts this diff could
have disturbed: R5 re-probed with a fresh build after generate.ts changed --
OPENAI_API_KEY absent from the entire .next output; R7's re-fetch-by-id still in place,
so a crafted POST still cannot shape the prompt; R8's ordering unchanged, with the RPC
still reachable only after generateHoroscope resolves.

Verified by execution at c3bf6fa:
- lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 149 tests across 15 files.
- next build exits 0; route table unchanged.
- The R5 probe above.

Notes, not conditions:
1. A reading saved for 2100-12-31 makes generateAndPersistHoroscope throw past its
   caller. I found this by reading the new code and then confirmed it by running it:
     computePromptAspects("2100-12-31", positions)
       -> THREW: Date must be between 1700-01-01 and 2100-12-31.
     generateAndPersistHoroscope(...) with that reading
       -> THREW PAST THE CALLER (not { ok: false })
   The cause is arithmetic: MAX_SUPPORTED_DATE is 2100-12-31, the fix adds one day to
   get the later snapshot, and computePositions rejects 2101-01-01. /chart's date input
   has max=2100-12-31, so a user can create exactly this reading and then press
   Generate. Because generateReadingHoroscope has no try/catch, that surfaces as Next's
   error page rather than the inline message every other failure path produces.
   I considered making this a condition and decided against it, and the reasoning is
   worth recording: R8 enumerates the failures it governs -- "an OpenAI error, timeout,
   or rate limit" -- and this is none of the three. The reading is left unchanged and
   no success state is shown, which are R8's other two demands. So no stated criterion
   is violated, and I am not going to invent one on the last gate before this ships.
   It is still a one-line fix and worth taking: either move buildReadingModel inside
   the existing try, or fall back to composeChart's own aspects when the later snapshot
   is out of range. The second is slightly better -- catching produces "Horoscope
   generation failed, try again", which is misleading advice for a date that will
   never work.
2. generate.ts's catch still discards the OpenAI error rather than logging it. Carried
   from round 1 unchanged, and the case is unchanged with it: this path fails for
   quota, rate limit and billing reasons, which are exactly the failures you diagnose
   from logs and cannot diagnose from the message the user sees. Sprint 16 promoted the
   identical point to a requirement; this one has money behind it.
3. set_reading_horoscope remains granted to anon, so the stored horoscope is not
   guaranteed to be model output -- anyone holding a reading id can write arbitrary
   text into it over the Data API. R3 requires that grant so it is not a deviation,
   and it is consistent with Sprint 4's link-is-the-access-control model. Recorded as
   a decision rather than a side effect; the tighter shape (grant to service_role,
   call with createAdminClient from the server action) remains available and would
   change nothing a user can see.
4. readingId is still interpolated into the redirect path unencoded. I re-checked: it
   cannot escape the origin, because the /reading/ prefix keeps even a //-leading value
   origin-relative. Not an open redirect. encodeURIComponent would match saveReading's
   own convention.
5. Accepted per Out of Scope and restated once more because this is the last static
   gate before it ships: a public unauthenticated button that costs money per press,
   no rate limiting, with the OpenAI spend cap and the kill switch as the only
   controls. The kill switch works without a redeploy, which is what makes that
   acceptable rather than reckless.

Cleared to ship at c3bf6fa. GroundTruth's second criterion -- that the generated prose
references placements actually in the payload -- now means something it did not mean
a commit ago: with applying flags correct, PRD §5's "Saturn in Leo squared Uranus in
Scorpio at less than a degree, still closing" is a sentence the model can actually
produce from the data it is given.

CONDITIONAL: GroundTruth live test, Sprint 17, commit
c3bf6fadf0a38044a0479ffc1921aab7b73e5e72.
Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app and the production Supabase Data
API via the anon client, 2026-08-23 ~01:29-01:32Z.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL. Three of four criteria verified, including the sprint's
actual proof. The fourth requires changing a production environment variable and
redeploying, which is Pipeman's lane, not mine. No defect found.

Deployed commit confirmed: /api/health/db reports
{"sha":"c3bf6fadf0a38044a0479ffc1921aab7b73e5e72","short":"c3bf6fa","isLocal":false},
migrationVersion 20260823004820_set_reading_horoscope.

CRITERION 1 -- on a reading with events, requesting generation produces a
horoscope that is persisted and survives a reload. PASS. This is the sprint's
actual proof: three independent sources in one row, verified from outside.
  Target: /reading/c78ee91d-53e1-4405-93ac-e1b4a0371ecd (1986-03-31), a reading I
  created during Sprint 16's test, already carrying real Wikipedia events with
  matchedYear true.
  POST the generate server action -> HTTP/2 303 back to the reading, 5137ms.
  Persisted columns read back through the anon get_reading_by_id RPC:
    horoscope_model: gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18
    horoscope_generated_at: 2026-08-23T01:29:14.168801+00:00
    horoscope: 1698 characters
  Survives reload: a fresh GET with no cookie jar returned 200 with the stored
  text rendered in the page, matching the persisted column. The control also
  changed from "Generate horoscope" to "Regenerate horoscope", which is R7's
  no-automatic-regeneration behaviour visible on the wire.

CRITERION 2 -- the generated text references planets, signs or aspects actually in
the payload. PASS, checked claim by claim rather than read for plausibility.
  The first generation made three specific, checkable astrological assertions. I
  computed each against the row's own stored positions:
    "an empowered Sun in Aries"        -> stored Sun Aries 10.48. TRUE.
    "Mercury danced in Pisces"         -> stored Mercury Pisces 17.99. TRUE.
    "the Moon in Sagittarius ... formed a powerful conjunction with Uranus"
       -> Moon 263.234 deg, Uranus 262.366 deg, separation 0.87 deg, well inside
          the 8 deg conjunction orb, and both in Sagittarius. TRUE.
    "Jupiter's square with Saturn"
       -> Jupiter 339.088 deg, Saturn 249.583 deg, separation 89.50 deg, orb 0.50
          against a 90 deg square with a 7 deg allowance. TRUE.
    "Saturn's retrograde"
       -> I expected this to be the catch. Saturn stations retrograde in late May
          in 1986, so my prior was that the model had invented it. The stored
          payload flags Saturn retrograde: true (along with Uranus and Pluto). The
          claim is grounded in the data the pipeline supplied. I checked before
          reporting rather than filing a finding I would have had to withdraw.
    "the balance of fire, earth, and water energies"
       -> stored signs give fire 5 (Sun, Venus, Moon, Saturn, Uranus), water 3
          (Mercury, Jupiter, Pluto), earth 2 (Mars, Neptune), air 0. The prose
          names exactly the three elements present and silently omits the one with
          no bodies in it. That is a derived fact from the payload, not a phrase
          that could be written blind.
    It also cites the Mexicana de Aviación Flight 940 crash by name -- the exact
    Wikipedia entry stored in this row's events column by Sprint 16.
  So the prose is drawing on all three sources in the row: Sprint 6's ephemeris,
  Sprint 16's Wikipedia payload, and Sprint 12's aspect vocabulary. Not a quality
  judgement, as the criterion says -- an accuracy check on whether the model
  ignored the pipeline. It did not.

  SECOND SAMPLE, because my brief requires re-running non-deterministic output
  rather than trusting one result. A later regeneration independently asserts
  "the Sun blazing in courageous Aries" (stored: Aries), "Mars ... nestled in
  steadfast Capricorn" (stored: Capricorn 1.68), and "the Moon danced in jovial
  Sagittarius and formed a conjunction with the rebellious Uranus" (stored: the
  same 0.87 deg conjunction). Grounded across both samples, not once by luck.

CRITERION 3 -- with HOROSCOPE_ENABLED set to disabled, no generation occurs and
the interface says so. NOT TESTED.
  HOROSCOPE_ENABLED exists as a non-sensitive Vercel variable on Production and
  Preview. Testing this criterion means: change the production value, redeploy so
  the change takes effect, exercise the path, change it back, redeploy again --
  four production operations, two of them deployments, on a live environment,
  with a revert I would have to be trusted not to forget.
  I do not deploy. That is Pipeman's job, and this is the same call I made on
  Sprint 5's rollback: I observe production changes, I do not perform them. I have
  an authenticated Vercel CLI and could run it; I am not going to on my own
  initiative.
  When Pipeman flips it, the check takes seconds and I will run it: load a reading
  that has no horoscope, confirm no OpenAI call happens, and confirm the interface
  states the feature is off rather than rendering a button that silently does
  nothing or an error that looks like a fault. R6 also says absent-or-any-other-
  value means enabled, so the disable value has to be the explicit one the code
  looks for -- worth confirming what that literal is before setting it, or the
  test will pass for the wrong reason.

CRITERION 4 -- a reading with events null still loads and does not error. PASS.
  /reading/f8d046f7-6432-4961-b996-d65c9f623a8e (the Sprint 14 fixture, events
  null) -> 200, heading "Reading for 1977-03-31", all ten bodies rendered, no
  error text anywhere in the page.

SECURITY PROPERTIES THIS SPRINT MUST NOT HAVE BROKEN -- all still hold.
  R4, Sprint 4's deny-update. Attacked it directly with the anon key:
    PATCH readings?id=eq.<id> setting horoscope to "TAMPERED BY GROUNDTRUTH" -> 204
    DELETE readings?id=eq.<id> -> 204
    unfiltered SELECT -> []
  Both writes are the same silent no-ops Sprint 4 documented, and I verified by
  reading the row back rather than trusting the status codes: the horoscope was
  still the 1698-character generated text, not "TAMPERED". No update policy was
  added to the table.
  R5, OPENAI_API_KEY server-side only. Fetched the reading page and every JS chunk
  it references and grepped for OPENAI_API_KEY and sk--prefixed strings: 0 hits.
  R7, regeneration overwrites in place. Two consecutive regenerations, 3253ms and
  3056ms, each replacing the single horoscope column and advancing
  horoscope_generated_at. No duplicate rows, no accumulation.
  Temperature 0.9 behaving as intended: three generations of the same reading
  produced three different texts (1698, 1618, 1677 characters, different opening
  sentences). Nondeterminism is the spec here, and it is real rather than a
  cached response replayed.

FINDING -- set_reading_horoscope accepts arbitrary text from anyone holding a
reading id. Not a defect against the spec; a consequence of it, worth stating
plainly before Sprint 18 renders this column.
  R3 requires the function be SECURITY DEFINER and granted to anon, and R4 makes
  it the entire write surface. That is exactly what shipped, and it works. The
  consequence is that the function performs no authorisation beyond knowing the
  row id:
    POST /rest/v1/rpc/set_reading_horoscope with the public anon key and
    {"reading_id": "<id>", "horoscope": "GT probe", "model": "gt"} -> 200, true
  and the row's horoscope became "GT probe" with horoscope_model "gt". Anyone with
  a reading's link can replace its horoscope with arbitrary content that never
  passed through OpenAI, and the page will render it exactly as if generated.
  Under Sprint 4's model -- no accounts, the unguessable link is the access
  control -- that is consistent: a link-holder can already do this to their own
  reading and cannot enumerate anyone else's. But it means the horoscope column
  is attacker-controlled content for any link that has been shared, and Sprint 18
  will render it. Escaping matters there; Sprint 6's date-echo path escapes
  correctly, so the pattern exists in this codebase already.
  I DID THIS BY ACCIDENT AND IT DESTROYED EVIDENCE. That probe overwrote the
  generated horoscope I had just recorded for criterion 1. Criterion 1's evidence
  survives because I had already captured the text, the model id, the timestamp
  and the reload check before probing -- but I should have run a write probe
  against a throwaway row rather than the one holding my evidence. I restored the
  row by regenerating through the product's own button, twice; "GT probe" is gone
  and the row now holds a real generated horoscope. Recording the sequence because
  the row's horoscope_generated_at no longer matches the generation I quote under
  criterion 1, and anyone reconstructing this later deserves to know why.

TEST DATA. No new rows this time -- I deliberately reused readings created in
earlier sprints rather than adding more. Running count of rows this role has left
in production remains nine. Three OpenAI generations were billed against the
project's key.

TOOLING CAVEAT: no Playwright MCP or Chrome extension in this session. All checks
are curl over HTTPS against production plus direct anon calls to the Supabase Data
API. The generate control is a no-JavaScript server-action form, so the path is
fully exercisable over plain HTTP; I have not observed the button in a browser or
any loading state it may show while the 3-5 second generation runs.

PASS: GroundTruth live test round 2, Sprint 17, commit
c3bf6fadf0a38044a0479ffc1921aab7b73e5e72.
Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app, 2026-08-23 ~01:45Z, with
HOROSCOPE_ENABLED=false set on production and redeployed by Pipeman.

VERDICT: PASS. Criterion 3 -- the only one outstanding from round 1 -- is now
verified, and it holds at the layer that matters rather than only in the UI.
Criteria 1, 2 and 4 passed in round 1 and are not re-litigated here; the code is
unchanged (same commit, redeployed to pick up the new environment value, confirmed
by /api/health/db still reporting sha c3bf6fa...).

CRITERION 3 -- with HOROSCOPE_ENABLED set to disabled, no generation occurs and
the interface says so. PASS, verified in three parts.

  1. THE INTERFACE SAYS SO. /reading/d8407973-a099-4b33-8bb2-ce6101bb5cb7 (a
     reading with events and no horoscope) renders, verbatim: "Horoscope
     generation is currently disabled." The generate form and its button are
     absent from the served HTML entirely -- no <button>, no $ACTION_ID. The page
     states the situation rather than showing a control that silently does
     nothing, which is what R6 asked for.

  2. NO GENERATION OCCURS -- AND THIS IS ENFORCED SERVER-SIDE, NOT JUST HIDDEN.
     A missing button is not a disabled feature. The server action still has an
     endpoint whether or not the page renders a form for it, so I called it
     directly with the action id captured in round 1, against a reading whose
     horoscope, horoscope_model and horoscope_generated_at were all null:
       POST /reading/d8407973-... with the generate action
       -> HTTP/2 303, location: /reading/d8407973-...?error=Horoscope%20generation
          %20is%20currently%20disabled.
       -> elapsed 523ms
     Round-1 generations against the same deployment took 3053-5137ms because they
     waited on OpenAI. 523ms is an order of magnitude faster and is the signature
     of a request that never made the call. The flag is checked before the API
     call, not after.
     The row was unchanged afterwards: horoscope None, horoscope_model None,
     horoscope_generated_at None -- read back through the anon RPC, not inferred
     from the redirect. No partial write, no timestamp advanced, nothing.

  3. THE MESSAGE REACHES THE USER. Following the redirect renders the error in the
     page rather than leaving it in the query string.

  DISABLING GATES GENERATION, NOT DISPLAY. The reading generated in round 1,
  /reading/c78ee91d-53e1-4405-93ac-e1b4a0371ecd, still renders its stored
  horoscope in full while the flag is off. Turning the feature off does not hide
  work already done, which is the correct behaviour and worth confirming rather
  than assuming -- a kill switch that also blanked existing readings would be a
  nasty surprise on the day someone flips it in anger.
